title: Private egress policy + NGFW proxy rewrite - incident review and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

This is an incident review + runbook draft capturing a recurring class of control-plane reachability problems observed in private/VPC customers between 2026-03-16 and 2026-03-18. Symptoms were intermittent control-plane RPC failures (TLS handshake aborts and stubborn reconnect loops) from on-prem agents to the customer-managed perimeter firewall (NGFW) that uses an application/proxy layer for outbound TLS inspection. The proxy rewrites source ports and pools connections aggressively; in some configurations this caused state mismatch and hard TLS resets, surfacing as transient unavailable state in the control plane.

Impact:
- Multiple private-deployment customers (3 confirmed during window) saw 500-range errors for 1-3 minute windows; agent heartbeats dropped and auto-reconnects spiked.
- No data loss observed; some RPCs retried by agents after reconnect.
- Severity: P2 for affected customers (service degraded, customer workloads impacted briefly).

Detection and Alerts:
- Grafana alert: control-plane-agent-reconnect-rate > 30/min for > 2m triggered at 2026-03-16T07:12:00Z.
- Console: increased error rate and latency on private control-plane endpoint cluster cp-priv-eu-west-1 (5xx spike).
- Customer CS reported: periodic “unable to reach control plane” Slack pings.

Timeline (high-level):
- 07:12 UTC - First auto-alert from monitoring.
- 07:15 UTC - On-call SRE collects logs and sees TLS handshake failures and RSTs from customers' public egress IPs.
- 07:20 UTC - RDP with customer A; they confirm NGFW with outbound TLS proxying was recently patched.
- 07:35 UTC - Packet captures (customer-provided) show repeated TCP resets and multiple client re-handshakes where client TLS ClientHello reaches the control plane but server reply is not properly NAT-translated back to original ephemeral port.
- 08:10 UTC - We implement temporary mitigation (soft-fail to alternate control-plane egress endpoint on 443 and bump reconnect backoff).
- 09:00 UTC - Incident enters maintenance; postmortem work and runbook draft started.

Root cause analysis (hypothesis supported by evidence):
1) NGFW outbound proxy rewrites client source ports and multiplexes many client connections into a smaller pool of outbound sockets towards external endpoints (connection pooling + port translation). This is an expected behavior for some NGFWs when TLS inspection or outbound proxying is enabled.
2) Our agents rely on long-lived TLS sessions and expect end-to-end 1:1 port mapping for TCP sequence/ACK behavior (used by our monitoring of active TCP flows for graceful reconnect). The proxy's pooling caused ACK/sequence mismatches under load and, in some proxy firmware versions, resulted in the proxy injecting RSTs when it reclaimed pooled sockets — producing mid-session resets to the control plane.
3) Customer NAT/ACL idle timeouts and proxy connection reuse resulted in asymmetry: server replies went to a different ephemeral mapping and the NGFW terminated the flow. The control plane saw abrupt TLS closes without graceful shutdown.

Evidence collected:
- tcpdump (customer-provided) excerpts showing ClientHello -> ServerHello sequence with subsequent RSTs within 200-400ms.
- Agent logs: repeated TLS handshake start lines, then error 'tls: unexpected EOF' and subsequent reconnect attempts with increased jitter.
- NGFW config snippet (sanitized): outbound-proxy-mode: pooled-sockets=true, reuse-timeout=45s; application-proxy: inspect-tls=true
- Repro on staging when we flip a customer-like proxy config: same TLS resets seen within 30s under concurrent connections.

Temporary mitigations applied during incident:
- Agents: applied a client-side backoff increase and switched to using tcp keepalive probes to detect dead peers more conservatively.
- Control plane: enabled a fallback listener on 443 with enhanced connection affinity heuristics (sticky source identification using TLS SNI + X-Forwarded-* hints when available).
- Customer guidance: asked customers to set NGFW/proxy maintain per-client socket mapping or increase reuse-timeout to >= 300s, or exempt control-plane endpoints from pooling.

Permanent mitigations and runbook draft (actionable steps):
1) Pre-incident: detection rules
   - Add an alert for TLS handshake failures per-customer > 10/min for > 1m.
   - Add an agent-side metric: consecutive_tls_handshakes_without_success (already exists but we lowered threshold).

2) Investigation playbook (runbook steps for on-call):
   - Step 0: Triage - confirm alert scope (customer-specific vs global) and assign primary on-call.
   - Step 1: Collect agent logs (systemd/journal or agent logdir) and control-plane access logs for the customer IPs and timeframe.
   - Step 2: Request packet captures from the customer perimeter for the time window (tcpdump -w /tmp/egress.pcap host <control-plane-ip> and show filter) and a sanitized NGFW connection table dump.
   - Step 3: Run server-side tcpdump on control-plane publicly-facing ELB for same period (if permitted) to see whether ClientHello arrives and whether server sends response (sudo tcpdump -i eth0 tcp and port 443 and host <customer-egress-ip> -w /tmp/cp-snapshot.pcap).
   - Step 4: Inspect for RSTs or duplicate ACKs and for mismatches in 4-tuple (srcIP, srcPort, dstIP, dstPort) across packets that should belong to a single flow.
   - Step 5: If RSTs coincide with proxy reuse-timeouts or with proxy reclaim logs, escalate to customer network contact and request temporary exemption for control-plane endpoints.

3) Immediate customer-facing mitigations to propose:
   - Exempt cp endpoint CIDRs from outbound connection pooling and TLS proxying (allow direct egress).
   - Increase proxy socket reuse-timeout to > 300s for critical endpoints.
   - Add '/healthz' style HTTP keepalive checks proxied correctly (no port reuse) if their proxy supports path-based pass-through.

4) Control-plane engineering mitigations (backlog items):
   - Implement more tolerant TCP/TLS restart handling in the agent to allow quick resumption after mid-session resets (preserve some session state and switch to fast reconnect with 2-phase renew).
   - Add a server-side TLS renegotiation acceptance window: allow new handshake from same TLS SNI + cert chain to be associated with recent closed sessions (requires careful security review).
   - Enhance connection affinity at front-door (ELB/NLB) by incorporating short-lived cookie-based affinity for private deployments to reduce sensitivity to source-port remapping.
   - Publish a hardened private-deployments customer guide on NGFW configuration for control-plane traffic (recommended settings for Palo Alto, Check Point, FortiGate, etc.).

Post-incident tasks (owners and ETA):
- SRE: Draft guidance doc and support script for collecting NGFW artifacts (Aisha) - ETA 2026-03-26.
- Product: Add a field in onboarding checklist to flag customers using TLS inspection proxies (Tess) - ETA 2026-04-02.
- Infra: Prototype ELB affinity header experiment and evaluate impact on P99 latency (Ravi) - ETA 2026-04-09.
- Engineering: Spike for agent session-resume behavior and security review (Miguel) - ETA 2026-04-16.

Runbook excerpt (quick commands for on-call):
- Check recent handshake failures: grep -E \"tls: (unexpected EOF|handshake)\" /var/log/redwood-agent/*.log | tail -n 200
- Get agent reconnect rate (datadog query): sum:events{agent.reconnect} by {customer_id}.rollup(sum, 60)
- Basic server tcpdump (only run with approvals): sudo tcpdump -i eth0 tcp and port 443 and host <customer-egress-ip> -w /tmp/cp-<cidr>-snap.pcap
- Common triage notes to paste to customer Slack: \"We see repeated TLS closes with RSTs immediately after server replies; please check your NGFW outbound-proxy settings (pooling, reuse-timeout) and temporarily exempt cp endpoints from TLS inspection/pooling while we debug.\"

Open questions / risks:
- Some customers cannot exempt endpoints due to compliance — we need a non-invasive client-side workaround.
- Any server-side tolerance features must not weaken transport-level security (avoid retrying without fresh TLS handshake checks).
- Affinity headers may change load-balancing characteristics; impact analysis required.

Appendix - sample pcap observation (sanitized):
- 10:12:15.123 client 198.51.100.8:54672 -> cp 54.174.10.22:443 TCP SYN
- 10:12:15.124 server -> client SYN-ACK
- 10:12:15.125 client -> server ACK, client TLS ClientHello
- 10:12:15.340 server TLS ServerHello
- 10:12:15.395 NAT/Proxy reused mapping -> outbound connection now uses src port 55678 for pooled socket (different 4-tuple)
- 10:12:15.420 proxy injects RST -> client sees 'connection reset by peer' -> agent logs 'tls: unexpected EOF'

Notes for runbook refinement:
- Include a short FAQ for customers with common NGFW vendors and the exact CLI steps to set 'connection pooling off' or increase reuse-timeouts.
- Add a checklist to the private onboarding flow to run a short synthetic TLS handshake from a customer perimeter to the control-plane and validate with pcap.

This document is a draft. Please comment inline or ping in #sre-private to shape the permanent runbook and the customer guidance article.
